claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance at elevated temperatures.
Approximately 0.5 at.% Y will be added to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr during casting.
Adding approximately 0.5 at.% Y during casting will produce homogeneous Y doping.
Y will segregate to the oxide/alloy interface.
Y addition will form dispersed Y2O3 particles within the developing oxide scale.
Y will pin grain boundaries in the oxide scale.
Improved scale stability and adhesion will limit oxide-scale spallation.
The Y-containing oxide scale will limit oxygen diffusion into the alloy substrate.
Limiting spallation and oxygen diffusion will mitigate oxidation and pesting.
Approximately 0.5 at.% Y will not alter the intrinsic equiatomic-alloy microstructure.
The Y-doped alloy will form a more protective and adherent oxide layer than undoped equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr during exposure in air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
The Y-doped alloy will retain its room-temperature tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
Undoped equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation and pesting during a 5-hour exposure in air at 800 °C.
Rapid oxidation and pesting of undoped equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr compromise its structural integrity and mechanical performance.
The proposed efficacy boundary is air exposure at 800 °C for 5 hours, excluding thermal cycling and longer exposure durations.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires mechanical properties to be retained without detrimental change, whereas the falsification rule can be read as requiring a statistically significant improvement in mechanical-property retention over the undoped control. Mere equivalence to the control would satisfy the stated non-detriment claim but could fail the stated falsification criterion.
